trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), handled null creation, used documented next_token(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), add_class(), get_last_error(), and get_updated_html(). Functional result was 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Main adherence deduction: it maintained a manual UL/OL stack instead of using the documented breadcrumb ancestry contract, so it is less idiomatic and depends on understanding virtual closer traversal.

Closest to the canonical documented pattern: structural processor, next_tag() opener scan, get_breadcrumbs() with the current element excluded, add_class(), and get_updated_html(). Functional result was 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Minor deduction: it does not check get_last_error() after the scan, so unsupported-markup/incomplete-scan policy is implicit rather than documented in the function.

Correct structural processor and documented API usage throughout: next_token(), get_token_type(), is_tag_closer(), get_tag(), get_breadcrumbs(), add_class(), get_last_error(), and get_updated_html(). Functional result was 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Slightly less idiomatic than trial-2 because it token-walks and filters tags where next_tag() would have been simpler; class_exists() is a harmless PHP guard, not an HTML API hallucination.

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases across the three trials: simple-ol-inside-ul, top-level-lists-untouched, ul-inside-ol, deep-descendant, existing-class-preserved, multiple-nested-levels, and mixed-document all passed in all trials. The docs worked well on the central decision: the Tag Processor overview says it has no tree awareness, while the HTML Processor overview says to use it for structure, containment checks, breadcrumbs, implied closers, and subtree walking. That led every trial to WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(). The Breadcrumbs and get_breadcrumbs() sections were sufficient for trials 2 and 3 to detect list ancestors, and the add_class()/get_updated_html() docs were sufficient to preserve existing classes and untouched bytes. The main near-miss was trial 1 constructing its own list stack even though breadcrumbs are the safer structural API; this happened to work because next_token() visits virtual closers, but the docs could more directly show the ancestor-anywhere pattern. Trial 2’s only notable omission was lack of a post-scan get_last_error() policy despite the HTML Support/create_fragment guidance that the processor may abort later on unsupported markup. The attribute null/true/empty and decoded-vs-raw text edge cases were not relevant to this task and did not affect any candidate.

doc_gaps.problem: The quick mutation example calls add_class() but does not show returning get_updated_html(), and get_updated_html() is not prominent in the HTML Processor method list even though it is the normal output API after inherited mutation methods.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Extend the Usage example to end with return $processor->get_updated_html(), and add a short inherited-mutation-output note near the method index: after set_attribute(), add_class(), remove_class(), or set_modifiable_text() on an HTML Processor, read the result with get_updated_html().

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain the full path and implicit HTML/BODY nodes, but do not provide a concise recipe for checking whether the current element has an ancestor anywhere above it.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general example that slices off the current token from get_breadcrumbs() and searches the remaining ancestors, e.g. for containment/ancestor checks where depth is not fixed.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe breadcrumb path matching and single-element wildcards, but the distinction between fixed path/suffix matching and arbitrary-depth ancestor matching is easy to miss.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an explicit note: breadcrumbs queries do not mean 'has this ancestor at any depth'; for arbitrary ancestors, scan tags and inspect get_breadcrumbs(), or use a depth-bounded walk when operating inside a known subtree.

doc_gaps.problem: Error/completeness guidance is present but scattered across structural scanning and serialization sections, while mutation tasks often end with get_updated_html().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact mutation-scan policy note: after a structural scan that determines edits, decide whether to fail closed on get_last_error() and whether paused_at_incomplete_token() matters; then return get_updated_html() only under that policy.
